'''Carl-Erik Sjöstedt''' (born 1900, died 1979) was a Swedish [[mathematician]], [[teacher]], and [[Philosophy|philosopher]]. Sjöstedt focused much of his work on the teaching of mathematics in the Swedish [[curriculum]], especially in the fields of geometry and logic. Sjöstedt was a follower of the Swedish philosopher [[Adolf Phalén]], and a supporter of ''Uppsala philosophy''. He also was a speaker and author in the [[constructed language]] [[Interlingue]], founding a national association for the language in 1928.

== Life ==

=== Early life and education ===
Sjöstedt was born on 31 July 1900 to [[Supervisor|foreman]] Karl August Sjöstedt and Matilda Åström in [[Eskilstuna]] [[parish]], [[Södermanland County]], Sweden. He began his education in the city, graduating in 1919. Sjöstedt would complete the rest of his education at [[Uppsala University]], gaining a [[Bachelor of Arts]] ({{Langx|sv|filosofie kandidat}}) in 1921, a [[Licentiate (degree)|licentiate]] in 1927, and becoming a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] in 1930. His thesis for the latter was [[Thesis defence|defended]] in 1929 and was on the subject of geometry.{{Sfn|(unknown)|1948}}

During his research, Sjöstedt met philosopher [[Adolf Phalén]], who would remain a friend of Sjöstedt's and influence his philosophical theories; Sjöstedt presented Phalén with a [[dissertation]] on the [[epistemology]] of geometry, which would be factored into a memorial to him in 1937. During the 1930s, Phalén, along with a group of other philosophers including Sjöstedt held private meetings to discuss the place of philosophy as a subject within the [[Education in Sweden|education system of Sweden]].{{Sfn|Kaijser|Andersson|2006}} After Phalén's death, Sjöstedt collected much of Phalén's unfinished and unpublished work, mainly concerning the history of the [[Theory of Knowledge|theory of knowledge]], and published it under the title ''Mindre Arbeten'' (''Minor Works'')''.''<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dahlquist |first=Thorild |title=Adolf K H Phalén |url=https://sok.riksarkivet.se/sbl/Presentation.aspx?id=7252 |access-date=2023-07-09 |website=Svenskt Biografiskt Lexikon}}</ref> Throughout his life, like Phalén, Sjöstedt was a proponent of {{Ill|Uppsalafilosofin|sv}} (Uppsala philosophy), countering opposing philosophies such as those of [[Hans Larsson]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Dymling |first=Carl |author-link=Carl Dymling |date=1939 |title=Svar till Rektor C. E. Sjöstedt |url=https://runeberg.org/pedagtid/1939/0166.html |journal=Pedagogisk Tidskrift |volume=4 |pages=162–163}}</ref>

=== Career ===
Sjöstedt worked as a teacher for much of his career, teaching at various [[private school]] until 1931, before lecturing in mathematics at the {{Ill|Jämtlands Gymnasium Wargentin|sv}} (then the ''Högre allmänna läroverket i Östersund;'' Higher General Education Agency in Östersund). In 1939, Sjöstedt  acted as [[headmaster]] at the {{Ill|Läroverk|sv}} (form of Swedish secondary school, similar to a [[Gymnasium (school)|gymnasium]]) in [[Borås]], [[Västergötland]]. After this, Sjöstedt was ''{{Ill|Undervisningsråd|sv}}'' (counsel of [[pedagogy]]) of the ''{{Ill|Skolöverstyrelsen|sv}}'' (former Swedish Board of Education) from 1940 until 1962.{{Sfn|Kaijser|Andersson|2006}}

Sjöstedt was an opponent of the 1950s movement to introduce [[Comprehensive school|comprehensive schools]], calling the movement "an educational utopia of colossal proportions"; his opposition was successful, as the 1962 Education Act replaced Sweden's previous schooling system which he had supported.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Husén |first=Torsten |date=1989 |title=The Swedish School Reform-Exemplary Both Ways |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/3099209 |journal=Comparative Education |volume=25 |issue=3 |pages=345–355 |doi=10.1080/0305006890250311 |jstor=3099209 |issn=0305-0068|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Sjöstedt later lead an inquiry into the role of [[Vocational school|vocational schools]],  supporting them as a default, as opposed to [[Upper Secondary School|Upper Secondary Schools]], but later resigned from the position.

=== Personal life ===
Aside from work in pedagogy and mathematics, Sjöstedt was a supporter of the [[international auxiliary language]] [[Interlingue]] (then known as Occidental), created by the Estonian [[Edgar de Wahl]]. Founding the {{Ill|Sved Occidental-Federation|ie}} (Swedish Occidental-Federation) in 1928,<ref>{{Cite book |last=(unknown) |url=https://runeberg.org/blaboken/1934/0238.html |title=BLÅ BOKEN |year=1934 |location=Stockholm |page=232 |language=sv}}</ref> Sjöstedt published several books in the language throughout his life. Sjöstedt published many articles in the organisation's magazine, ''Li Sved Occidentalist'' (''The Swedish Occidentalist''), as well as the magazine [[Cosmoglotta]]. 

Sjöstedt married Svea Augusta Malmberg on 7 July 1927,{{Sfn|Kaijser|Andersson|2006}} and died on 8 February 1979 in the parish of [[Uppsala Cathedral]], [[Uppsala County]], aged 78.{{Sfn|(unknown)|1948}}
== Works ==
Sjöstedt wrote several [[Textbook|textbooks]] about geometry, publishing courses for high schools in 1936 and 1938, as well as a series of other textbooks through the 1950s. Sjöstedt also wrote for the Swedish journal [[Natur & Kultur]] from 1947. Aside from these, Sjöstedt also published several books about geometry theory and philosophy, including ''De filosofiska problemens historia'' (''The history of [[philosophical problems]]'') in 1936, for use in teaching high school philosophy, alongside ''Översikt av den formella logiken'' (''An overview of [[formal logic]]'').{{Sfn|Kaijser|Andersson|2006}} Other works included:

* ''Occidental - de internatuinella ordens språk,'' 1928
* ''Dubbel Occidental''-''Ordbok'', 1930 (in Occidental, Swedish)
* ''Projektiv geometri,'' 1932, second edition published 1947
* ''Geometriens axiomsystem'', 1937

* ''Zur Erkenntnistheorie der Geometrie,'' 1937 (in German)
* ''Icke-euklidisk geometri'', 1945
* ''Filosofisk läsebok'', 1950
* ''Le Axiome de Paralleles de Euclides a Hilbert'', a mathematical encyclopaedia of around 1000 pages; 1968 (in Occidental)
* ''Vocabularie mathematic in interlingue: Con traduction in angles, frances e german'', 1970; published in [[Natur och Kultur]]. (in Occidental, English, French, and German)
